analysis: The PR changes only docs/operations/provider-release.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04) and edits the release SDK selection sentence at line 611 (SDK 27.0 / Swift 6.4 to SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2, Xcode 27.2). I read all three units, base lines 467-1005 and head lines 1-466, against the threat model. No code, workflow, script, secret handling, signing, attestation, or coordinator contract is modified. The documented controls are unchanged: trusted-source gates, the Developer ID designated requirement, final-bytes hashing, durable official identity and revocation, tag-gated prod, the PROD_*/DEV_* secret separation, and the cluster runtime facts flow. The document says the final recorded SDK must match the selected SDK, so the doc edit does not weaken a stated check. It is a doc-only statement of toolchain policy. I cannot verify from the supplied evidence that the workflows, the action, and scripts/install-macos-github-cli.sh or the SDK-pin checks actually select SDK 27.2. The head side of line 611 and the surrounding head text were not supplied, so only the patch excerpt shows the new wording. If the docs drift from the workflow, that is documentation drift only. The toolchain bump itself is outside the supplied diff. A reviewer of the actual workflow changes should confirm that SDK pin, cache keys, qualification and recorded-SDK matching are consistent. The remaining prose (staging, dev-branch lane, cluster runtime rollout) is unchanged context and not newly introduced. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumptions were identified for T-034, T-054, or TB-011 from this change.
